description: Audit cron and scheduled-job monitoring coverage, set up Watchgoose checks for one job or a batch, review monitoring health and triage missed runs.

interface.longDescription:
Watchgoose is cron job and heartbeat monitoring for scheduled tasks: cron jobs, systemd timers, Kubernetes CronJobs, backups and recurring scripts. When a job runs late, fails or never runs, Watchgoose alerts you through email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, PagerDuty, webhooks and more.

Connect one Watchgoose project and ask about your monitoring in plain language: check status, schedules and status history, plus recent pings and alert integrations on read-and-write connections. Read-only access is the default. With explicit read-and-write consent you can also create, update, pause, resume and delete checks.

Five built-in workflows:
- Coverage audit: sort the scheduled jobs in a repository into monitored, confirmed gaps and unknown coverage.
- Job setup: draft check settings and a heartbeat wrapper for one job.
- Batch setup: create checks for many jobs after a single approval.
- Health review: spot paused checks, checks that are not armed yet, possible alert routing gaps and jobs running close to their grace time.
- Missed-run triage: summarize what happened when a check goes down.

The workflows never run your jobs or send test pings, and nothing changes without your approval. Requires a Watchgoose account; you sign in when you connect.
defaultPrompt: Find cron jobs and scheduled tasks in this repository that have no Watchgoose monitoring.
Set up Watchgoose monitoring for my nightly database backup cron job.
Which of my Watchgoose checks are down or late, and what happened?
